items.summary: The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, a reduction from September but a level economists said is still uncomfortably high.

scraped.title: Here's the inflation breakdown for October 2026 — in one chart
scraped.description: The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, a reduction from September but a level economists said is still uncomfortably high.
scraped.author: Greg Iacurci
scraped.h1: Here's the inflation breakdown for October 2026 — in one chart
scraped.body_text:
Inflation throttled back in October from its blistering pace in September amid a more moderate rise in gasoline prices, but remained high as categories like food and housing put upward pressure on consumer prices.

The consumer price index, an inflation barometer, rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, after adjusting for seasonal factors, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday. That's down from 0.6% in September but higher than the 0.3% that economists expected .

"It's uncomfortably high," said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's. "The Fed's not going to be happy about it. It certainly makes it more likely we get another rate increase in December."

The Federal Reserve uses inflation data to guide its interest rate policy. The U.S. central bank raised rates in September amid a recent pickup in inflation, which economists largely attribute to the war in Iran . It held rates steady at its last meeting in October.

Economists generally assess a measure known as "core" CPI — which strips out volatile food and energy prices — to examine underlying inflation dynamics in the U.S. economy.

That core metric rose 0.3% in October, as it also did in September and August. A consistent monthly reading around 0.2% would be more in line with the Fed's 2% annual inflation target, Zandi said.

Inflation has been above the Fed's target for more than five years.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics didn't report an annual inflation figure in the latest CPI report because of the lengthy federal government shutdown that happened a year ago. That shutdown, which ran from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, disrupted the agency's typical data collection , and it didn't release an inflation report for October 2025.

"Investors do not need year-over-year figures to see that this was a hot inflation report and that prices are not on a sustainable path back toward the Fed's 2% target," Jason Pride, chief of investment strategy and research at Glenmede, a wealth management firm, wrote in an e-mail Tuesday.

"It would have taken exceptional evidence of disinflation to dissuade the Fed from raising rates in December, and this report delivered the opposite," he wrote.

Economists pointed to four big reasons for the hotter-than-expected CPI reading.

Perhaps the largest contributor to the outsized inflation reading in Tuesday's CPI report was housing, Zandi said.

Housing is the largest component of CPI, and movements in the category strongly influence the index's month-to-month reading, he said.

The "shelter" CPI index rose 0.3% in October, accounting for over 30% of the CPI increase, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Zandi said he doesn't expect that dynamic to persist, however, because it's not consistent with the trajectory of market rents in the U.S.

"It does feel like we have a high level of monthly volatility" in the CPI data, he said. "It's all over the map month to month."

But economists said broader factors are putting upward pressure on prices, too.

"Core inflation today reflects three outsized shocks: tariffs, energy prices, and AI-related demand," Josh Hirt, senior U.S. economist at Vanguard Group, an asset manager, wrote in an e-mail Tuesday.

The Iran war has raised oil prices, pushing up prices for fuels like gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, which are refined from crude oil, economists said.

Gasoline prices rose 1% in October, a significant pullback after a 9.1% monthly increase in September, CPI data showed.

While diesel prices have retreated from recent record highs , they remain elevated and could spill more broadly into the U.S. economy in the coming months, economists said.

"Diesel prices have a really slow pass-through to all the areas of CPI, given it affects transportation costs," said Thomas Ryan, a senior North America economist at Capital Economics.

"These things take time," Ryan said. "It'll be an inflationary impetus for at least the next three to six months, I suspect."

There was some evidence of that broader percolation of diesel prices in October, such as in food prices, Zandi said. Higher diesel prices add to the cost of transporting food to the grocery store shelves, he said.

Food prices rose 0.5% in October after an unchanged reading in September, according to CPI data.

The run-up in jet fuel costs has also led airlines to raise their ticket prices, economists said. Airfares climbed 0.4% in October, after monthly increases of 1.2%, 2.7% and 3.8% in the preceding months, respectively, according to the CPI report.

Meanwhile, the inflationary impact of tariffs imposed by the Trump administration should fade by the end of the year, assuming the White House doesn't renew its push for more import taxes, Zandi said.

Certain categories of physical goods, like toys, furniture, and appliances, saw elevated inflation rates in October, likely because businesses have passed on tariff costs to consumers, he said.

The buildout of data centers that power artificial intelligence has driven up prices for electricity and consumer electronics, economists said.

Those data centers have led to a shortage of technology equipment, such as memory chips used in household electronic products like iPhones, Ryan said.

items.title: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
items.summary: The allegations against Jensen Huang have brought new attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China.

scraped.title: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
scraped.description: The allegations against Jensen Huang have brought new attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China.
scraped.author: Katie Tarasov
scraped.h1: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
scraped.body_text:
In this article

Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission on Sunday to an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, the chipmaker's relationship to China is about to come under intense scrutiny in Washington, D.C.

Since October 2022, when the Biden administration announced sweeping controls to limit China's ability to obtain advanced U.S. chips, Nvidia has seen its business diminish in the world's second-largest economy. Months after an even stricter set of rules was implemented by the Trump administration, Huang said in October 2025, "We are 100% out of China."

The recent allegations against Huang, while throwing the chipmaker into crisis, have also brought attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China, where its business once flourished. Of particular interest is whether restricted Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies through customers like Singapore-based Megaspeed , the company linked to Alice Huang.

The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear.

Jensen Huang has been closely aligned with President Donald Trump during his second administration, helping advise the White House on artificial intelligence safety regulations, while also pushing for looser restrictions on selling AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia would be allowed to ship its H200 chips to China, provided the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales. In March, Huang told reporters that Nvidia had "received purchase orders, and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing ."

Huang was a last-minute addition to the roster of tech executives who joined Trump on a trip to China in May, after the president was briefed on intelligence concerns, according to the Times .

"In 35 years, I haven't seen a chip CEO with this much direct influence on export policy," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO at Moor Insights & Strategy, in an email.

Since last week's midterm elections that included sweeping victories across the country for Democrats, the mood in Washington has changed. Three House committees have requested closed-door briefings with the Nvidia CEO about his relationship with Megaspeed.

Democratic lawmakers, who are about to take power in the House and Senate, have said publicly that Congress will investigate and seek answers. Trump said Monday that he was "amazed" by the allegations and that Huang told him he "had no idea that she was a spy." The FBI is now looking into the issue, Trump said at a White House briefing.

It's been a long four years for Nvidia in China.

Before the initial export controls in 2022, China made up nearly a quarter of Nvidia's revenue. Nvidia responded to the Biden-era restrictions by redesigning some of its products to comply with the new regulations.

"It was a turbulent month or so as the company went upside down to re-engineer" the products, Huang told CNBC in a 2023 interview. Still, he was confident the company could continue selling chips to China. "I think we're going to be just fine in the ability to serve the customers there," he said.

After the Biden administration tightened export restrictions again, Nvidia redesigned another AI graphics processing unit for China, the H20. Following reports that Chinese model developer DeepSeek was using restricted Nvidia chips, the Trump administration limited sales of H20. Nvidia revealed it would incur $5.5 billion in costs related to canceled orders for the redesigned chip.

However, despite saying in its forecasts that "we're assuming 0% for China," the company maintained business in the region. In the last fiscal year, Nvidia reported that about 9% of its revenue came from China, including Hong Kong, although that includes revenue from segments outside of restricted data center chips, such as gaming, auto and industrial. Nvidia's China revenue was 8% in the most recent quarter.

A report in May from short seller Culper Research alleged Nvidia's China exposure was much higher. The firm said that more than 20% of Nvidia's fiscal 2026 compute revenue was driven by China, supported by "illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries," according to the report.

A loophole allows Chinese companies to rent Nvidia GPUs in data centers, even when they're restricted from buying them outright. For example, a Chinese company could lease Nvidia computing power in Europe by renting server capacity from a non-Chinese neocloud or data center operator that's exempt from export controls.

Nvidia didn't respond to a request for comment for this story.

Megaspeed , an Nvidia customer based in Singapore, has been accused of diverting its own supply of Nvidia's restricted AI chips to Chinese companies. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing and said inspections found no evidence of violations.

In 2025, Nvidia changed the way it reported regional sales to categorize by customer headquarters, instead of by where the products were billed. Nvidia also stopped reporting Singapore sales during the same period.

"Whether Blackwell chips reached China is a Megaspeed question that predates this week," said Moorhead, pointing to Bloomberg reporting in December 2025 that found Megaspeed had imported 50,000 more Nvidia chips than Nvidia tallied in its data centers.

In 2025, a House Select Committee opened an investigation into whether China's DeepSeek operates on Nvidia's chips.

A separate investigation by the U.S. Commerce Department was centered on Megaspeed. That probe was abruptly transferred to the Justice Department, the Times reported , following an email from Nvidia's general counsel to the Commerce Department seeking information about the investigation.

The restrictions aren't just coming from the U.S. China has continued to limit the amount of Nvidia chips it will allow into the country, keeping Nvidia's China sales numbers down. The U.S. has licensed H200 sales to Alibaba , Tencent, ByteDance and other Chinese companies, but Beijing hasn't approved large-scale imports, Moorhead told CNBC. Nvidia said H200 shipments to China made up less than 1% of data center revenue for the quarter that ended in July.

Moorhead expects more export control legislation to pass as a result of the latest turmoil. Proposals could allow Congress oversight of chip export licenses or require chipmakers to install security mechanisms to track the location of chips to determine if they've found their way to China.

"Every China license now gets read through this story," Moorhead said. "Jensen has been Nvidia's lead voice on China, and that voice is weaker."

— CNBC's Kif Leswing and Seema Mody contributed reporting to this report.

Correction: Three House committees have requested closed-door briefings with the Nvidia CEO about his relationship with Megaspeed. An earlier version misstated the time element.

scraped.title: Schumer accuses Trump of defending Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at cost of national security
scraped.description: Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., the Republican chairman of the Select Committee on China and told CNBC he expects answers about Jensen Huang's relationship.
scraped.author: Dan Mangan,Justin Papp,Garrett Downs,Josephine Rozzelle
scraped.h1: Schumer accuses Trump of defending Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at cost of national security
scraped.body_text:
In this article

Democratic leader Sen. Charles Schumer ripped President Donald Trump on Tuesday for defending embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the expense of U.S. national security.

"The press reports that Trump was briefed more than a year ago that Nvidia's CEO was having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Trump didn't do anything – anything – about it," Schumer, D-N.Y., said on the Senate floor.

"Can you believe that?" said Schumer, the Senate's minority leader.

Schumer's broadside came on the heels of New York Times reports that Trump had been briefed about Huang's extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang — whom U.S. intelligence concluded was a spy for China — and opted not to do anything about it.

Trump suggested to reporters on Monday that he only recently learned of the allegations about Alice Huang, and the president commented Monday that he "really" believes Jensen Huang's claim to him directly that he had no idea Alice Huang was a spy.

"One of our most important companies that is involved in national security, and the CEO might be having an affair with a Chinese spy, and Trump did nothing about it," Schumer said Tuesday.

"What a dereliction of duty. He's supposed to protect America, not China, not his friends," Schumer said. "Trump has been busy trying to defend Jensen Huang when he ought to be defending our national security. It's that simple, it's obvious."

Schumer's comments escalated growing bipartisan concern in Congress about the Nvidia CEO, whose company makes advanced chips that power artificial intelligence in the U.S. and China's race to dominate that technology.

Schumer noted that Trump earlier this year invited Huang to join him on a state visit to Beijing, and that he took Huang's advice by granting the People's Republic of China "access to some of our most advanced AI chips."

Nvidia also donated $25 million to Trump's controversial White House ballroom project, the Democrat said.

"Despite talking a big game, Trump continues to show a troubling resistance to confront China on AI and to protect American national security," Schumer said. "I've been saying it for years: our cutting-edge AI chips are too valuable to fall into the hands of potential adversaries."

Schumer in his speech called on Republicans to join Democrats in passing several pieces of legislation — the AI OVERWATCH Act, the MATCH Act, and the Chip Security Act — which he said would "cut off China's access to advanced American technology."

"We also need answers on Nvidia's influence campaign and how [it] affected the Trump administration's national security decisions, including the loosening – the loosening – of key export controls," Schumer said. "We need a full accounting for Trump's failure to address foreign espionage in the American tech industry."

CNBC has requested comment from the White House about Schumer's remarks.

The remarks came nearly a week after Democrats won enough Senate and House races nationwide to take majority control of both chambers in January. Schumer hopes to be selected majority leader.

Regardless of which Democrats are tapped to serve as majority leaders in both chambers, the party will have the ability to launch investigations into Nvidia and Huang.

Earlier Tuesday, Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., said on CNBC's " Squawk Box " that Congress needs to "get to the bottom" of Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang.

Moolenaar, who chairs the House Permanent Select Committee on China, said he wants to know whether Huang shared privileged information with a Chinese spy; whether Huang was influenced to lobby against preventing chip sales to China; and whether China was given preference in purchasing Nvidia's limited supply of advanced chips.

And he urged a thorough internal investigation of Huang.

"If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work because people have to have confidence," Moolenaar said.

"We're dealing with the country, the Chinese Communist Party that is a foremost adversary, that's funding wars and supporting Russia, supporting Iran, North Korea," he said. "And we have basically a Cold War race with technology. We cannot allow the premier company at the forefront of this to, in some way, be irresponsible."

Congressional scrutiny of Huang's affair has intensified since members returned to Washington on Monday, a day after Nvidia announced it was opening an independent investigation of Jensen Huang's conduct.

Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, raised concerns that the scandal could plague talks over export controls for advanced AI chips. "It's important not to have a personal scandal interfere with the substantive policy discussion about to what degree we should be allowing the export of cutting edge chips to our geopolitical competitors like China," Obernolte told CNBC. "I hope this isn't a distraction because that's a very important conversation that needs to happen."

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., said in a press conference on Monday that "we're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of national security"

Moolenaar co-authored a letter with Florida Rep. Brian Mast and Arkansas Rep. Rick Crawford on Nov. 5 asking Huang to appear before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and House Select Committee on Intelligence. Mast chairs the foreign affairs panel, and Crawford chairs intelligence.

"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the three Republicans wrote.

Mast said Tuesday he did not know whether Huang had responded to the letter he authored with Moolenar and Crawford demanding the tech CEO brief them. "I can't say that I've heard an answer back yet that," Mast told reporters at the Capitol. Mast then rattled off a list of questions he has for Huang, including where the company has been selling chips, what Megaspeed may have been using them for, who has been remotely accessing Nvidia chips and what information was passed between Huang and the potential spy. "Obviously questions relating to his relationship and what information was or was not passed about anything," Mast said when asked what he wants answered.

Mast said he "can't say it would hurt" to hear from the Commerce Department as well, noting he speaks regularly to the Bureau of Industry and Security. "So that's obviously something that falls directly under Commerce," he said

items.title: Jury convicts Canadian woman who ‘answered ISIS’s call’
items.summary: The trial of Ammara Amjad was a test of whether Canada could bring to justice women who served the Islamic State.

scraped.title: Jury convicts Canadian woman who ‘answered ISIS’s call’ | Globalnews.ca
scraped.description: The trial of Ammara Amjad was a test of whether Canada could bring to justice women who served the Islamic State.
scraped.h1: Jury convicts Canadian woman who ‘answered ISIS’s call’
scraped.body_text:
Want to discuss? Please read our Commenting Policy first.

Comment

Name

Δ

3 comments

Send all of them back, terrorists

Why did Canada bring them back with our tax dollars?

Thankfully the jury has more intelligence than the judge Be interesting to see whether the judge goes easy during sentencing or respects the juries decision

A Canadian woman who spent four years with ISIS and married two of its fighters is guilty of terrorism, a jury in Brampton, Ont. ruled on Tuesday.

Ammara Amjad, 32, was the first woman to go on trial in Canada for her role in the Islamic State in Syria as it committed widespread atrocities.

The case was a test of whether Canada could bring to justice the women who played support roles in ISIS as wives and mothers but were not armed fighters.

The jury began deliberations on Monday and returned after one day to find Amjad guilty of participating in, or contributing to, the activities of a terrorist group.

A former York University student and Walmart employee, Amjad was living a life of “comfort” in Ontario when ISIS summoned women to Syria, according to the Crown.

The Pakistan-born Canadian flew to Turkey in March 2015, crossed into ISIS territory and remained with the terror group until she was captured four years later.

“She answered ISIS’s call,” the Crown argued in its closing arguments on Friday, as the two week trial came to an end in a courtroom north of Toronto.

Amjad faces a possible sentence of ten years in prison. She was not detained during the trial, having been released on bail after she was charged in 2023.

She did not testify in her defence and her lawyer did not present any evidence, instead arguing the Crown had not proved what Amjad did in Syria.

European and American courts have convicted dozens of women who flocked to Syria to live under ISIS rule. As recently as Oct. 27, a U.S. woman was convicted .

But Canadian authorities have struggled to prosecute citizens for their part in overseas terrorist groups, citing the challenges of collecting evidence in foreign conflict zones.

At least 11 Canadian women suspected of joining ISIS were caught in Syria. Nine were repatriated by the government from 2021 to 2023, but only three have been charged.

Oumaima Chaouay of Montreal pleaded guilty to participating in ISIS last year. She was sentenced to one day, on top of the 110 days she had spent in pre-trial custody.

Kimberly Polman pleaded guilty to the same charge in October. The B.C. resident, who allegedly received weapons training in Syria, is scheduled for sentencing on Nov 30.

Amjad opted to let a jury decide her fate, turning the case into a test of whether Canada could hold to account women accused of joining the terror group.

The defence depicted her as a naive youth who went to Syria to join her boyfriend, and argued that prosecutors had not shown she had knowingly contributed to ISIS.

“Do not convict her because of the place where she lived. Do not convict her because of who she married,” her lawyer Ayeman Kenaway told the jurors.

But the Crown said that not all terrorists carried weapons, and the evidence showed Amjad had participated in ISIS by taking on the domestic tasks it assigned to her.

Amjad married an ISIS fighter, Bilal Khan of Mississauga, Ont. When he died, she married another, British citizen Hamza Parvez , with whom she had two children.

She was on the ISIS payroll, espoused its ideology to family and friends in Canada, and pestered them repeatedly for money, according to the Crown.

“She fulfilled the role of the wife of ISIS fighters and mother to the next generation,” the Crown said, arguing Amjad knew ISIS was a terrorist group before she joined.

“Amjad made a considered, deliberate decision to migrate to Syria and fulfill the role of women in ISIS for the purpose of helping ISIS carry out its terrorist activities.”

Canadian women left B.C., Alberta, Ontario and Quebec to join ISIS after the terror group seized parts of Syria and Iraq that it proclaimed a puritanical Islamic State.

The RCMP was unaware of Amjad until she was captured in March 2019 near Baghouz, the Syrian town where the hardcore of ISIS made their last stand.

The Integrated National Security Enforcement Team was unable to locate any record of her travel because so much time had elapsed since she had left Canada.

But the investigators found she had renewed her Canadian passport in March 2015, bought a plane ticket to Turkey, and allegedly left her parents to pay her credit card debt.

At the time of what she called her “hijra,” Arabic for migration, ISIS was the topic of blanket news coverage, and had left no doubt about what it stood for.

It had called for terrorist attacks in Canada, beheaded prisoners on video, massacred Iraq’s Yazidi minority and abducted young girls to serve as sex slaves.

The abhorrent abuses had led Canada to join an international military coalition assembled to fight the terrorist group, which had emerged from the Al Qaeda branch in Iraq.

“By 2015, ISIS was a notorious terrorist group. It was a listed terrorist entity in Canada for a year before Ms. Amjad made her way to the ISIS territory,” the Crown said.

It was “completely implausible and unbelievable” that Amjad was unaware of that, according to the Crown, adding there was no evidence she was compelled to join ISIS.

“This was a woman committed to her own choices from the beginning to the end, not someone who was forced to do anything against her will,” the Crown said.

The evidence collected by police was described by the judge as circumstantial, but included documents on Parvez that were found in Syria, and which the FBI shared with the RCMP.

The U.K. government, meanwhile, notified the RCMP it had revoked Parvez’s citizenship after he left London, where he was born, to join ISIS, the Crown said.

The RCMP also found thousands of WhatsApp text and audio messages on a phone seized during a search at Amjad’s parents’ house.

The messages show that, while in Syria, Amjad had told her family and friends she was happy, had done the right thing and they had a religious duty to follow in her footsteps.

In November 2015, she contacted Khan’s family in Ontario to announce he’d been “martyred” in a Russian airstrike. As proof, she allegedly sent a photo of his body.

She allegedly later called them back to ask for permission to marry another ISIS fighter, Parvez, a British-Pakistani extremist.

The defence challenged the RCMP translations of her messages, which were mostly in Urdu, and at one point argued unsuccessfully for a mistrial.

Amjad made no effort to leave ISIS until the terror group was surrounded by U.S.-backed Syrian-Kurdish fighters, who captured her and Parvez in March 2019.

For the next four years, she lived at the Al Hol and Al Roj detention camps for the families of ISIS fighters, until Global Affairs Canada secured her release in April 2023.

Her sentencing has been scheduled for Feb. 2.

items.title: Red hot U.S. inflation reading dials up interest rate worries on markets
items.summary: U.S. stocks were under pressure Tuesday after a report showed inflation was worse across the country last month than economists expected.

scraped.description: U.S. stocks were under pressure Tuesday after a report showed inflation was worse across the country last month than economists expected.
scraped.h1: Red hot U.S. inflation reading dials up interest rate worries on markets
scraped.body_text:
Instructions:

Want to discuss? Please read our Commenting Policy first.

Comment

Name

Δ

2 comments

I have a feeling that sometime in early 2029, GIobaIist News will stop giving bi-weekly updates on the US economy.

Uncertainty causes inflation now. I’d like to see the math behind that fodder on a spreadsheet.

U.S. stocks were under pressure Tuesday after a report showed inflation was worse across the country last month than economists expected.

The S&P 500 fell 0.7 per cent and gave back some of its big rally from the day before. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 333 points, or 0.6 per cent, as of 10:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 0.8 per cent lower.

U.S. inflation was higher than expected last month, signaling that rising prices that powered sweeping Democratic victories in last week’s midterm elections will continue posing challenges for the White House and the Federal Reserve.

The consumer price index rose 0.4 per cent from September to October, the Labor Department said Tuesday, down from 0.6 per cent the previous month. Economists polled were expecting inflation to rise by 0.3 per cent. The government did not report a yearly inflation rate because last year’s government shutdown meant no data was released for October 2025.

Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 0.3 per cent, the same as the preceding month. Both figures were a tenth of a point higher than forecast.

Pressure from the bond market undercut stocks following the discouraging report on inflation. People had to pay prices for groceries, electricity and other costs of living that were even higher last month than economists expected. That could push the Federal Reserve to hike its main interest rate at its next meeting in December and beyond.

Higher interest rates can help rein in inflation, but they do so by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money and by slowing the overall economy. Higher rates also make investors less willing to pay high prices for stocks and other investments.

One Fed official even hinted the central bank may increase the federal funds rate by double the typical amount next month because of how high inflation has remained for years.

Speaking in London before the inflation report was released, Fed Gov. Christopher Waller said “a stronger policy move may be needed” if the report showed an important underlying measure of inflation rose by 0.3 per cent from September.

In that case, he said the Fed should consider hiking the federal funds rate by half a percentage point rather than the typical quarter point. Moving by only the usual amount could “put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.”

Shortly afterward, Tuesday’s inflation report showed that the underlying measure of inflation Waller was worried about was exactly 0.3 per cent, the threshold he had set. It’s the Fed’s job to keep inflation under control, along with keeping the job market strong.

That sent yields jumping in the bond market as traders upped their forecasts for coming hikes to rates by the Fed.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 4.99 per cent from 4.88 per cent late Monday. It’s a notable move for the bond market, and the yield helps set where rates are for mortgages and other loans going to U.S. households and businesses.

The 10-year Treasury yield had been dropping since early October, when it topped 5.30 per cent as worries spiked about high inflation, higher interest rates, the U.S. government’s big debt and other concerns.

Tuesday’s jump in yields came even though oil prices fell again. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil sank 2.4 per cent to US$90.31. President Donald Trump said late Monday that the war in Iran, which sent oil prices much higher, “militarily is effectively over.”

Brent’s price has been falling from more than $112 at the start of the month amid uncertainty about what will happen with the war with Iran.

Jumps in Treasury yields push downward on prices for all kinds of stocks, and they can particularly hurt companies in the real-estate business.

Higher mortgage rates can keep potential customers away from homebuilders, for example, and Lennar fell five per cent for one of the sharper losses in the S&P 500.

Rival homebuilders also fell, including drops of 4.3 per cent for D.R. Horton and 4.3 per cent for PulteGroup. Builders FirstSource, which sells crown mouldings, cabinets and other products to homebuilders, sank 5.3 per cent.

The single heaviest weight on the S&P 500 was Nvidia, which fell 5.3 per cent. It’s been under pressure since its board announced an investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, who admitted to a relationship with a woman who, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for China.

It’s also been swinging amid broader worries that have knocked the artificial-intelligence industry around recently. Democratic victories in statehouses across the country last week raised concerns about possible restrictions on construction of AI data centres. That built on top of already longstanding worries that AI stock prices had shot too high and were in a bubble.

Outside of Nvidia, other stocks in the AI industry were mixed. GE Vernova, which is helping to power AI data centres, dropped 7.2 per cent. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers, fell 2.3 per cent after flipping between gains and losses earlier in the morning.

But Advanced Micro Devices climbed 2.6 per cent. CoreWeave, a company that rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, also held up better. It added 0.8 per cent.

The recent shakiness for AI-related stocks had raised questions about whether Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, may delay its initial public offering of stock.

But Anthropic said in a filing with U.S. regulators on Tuesday that it’s looking to sell its stock at a price valuing the company at roughly $1.3 trillion. That would make it one of the most valuable companies on Wall Street, worth more than Walmart, JPMorgan Chase, ExxonMobil or Coca-Cola.

In stock markets abroad, indexes rose across much of Europe and Asia.

South Korea’s Kospi jumped 4.4 per cent for one of the world’s biggest gains on strength for its two tech giants that have benefited from the AI boom, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.

scraped.body_text:
Instructions:

Comment

Name

Δ

1 comment

She will find some way to cash in on it

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry made their first public appearance on Tuesday since her father’s arrest on suspicion of possessing images of child sexual abuse .

Harry urged tech companies to be more transparent about issues involving children as he spoke at the European Parliament in Brussels during the opening of a memorial to children who have died as the result of harm suffered on social media.

The Lost Screen Memorial features replicas of oversized smartphones with the photo of a child on each home screen.

The Duchess of Sussex was originally scheduled to speak alongside Harry but withdrew because she was not “strong enough emotionally,” a person familiar with her reasoning told The Associated Press.

Meghan still accompanied her husband to the event and they were photographed arriving at the European Parliament.

During his speech, Harry appeared emotional as he told social media companies to avoid showing children content they would not show their own children.

“I’m not here as an expert or a politician. I’m here as a father, my wife, as a mother and together, as a couple who stand alongside parents like Sandra, Megan and Sewell — in New York, Los Angeles, Geneva and now Brussels. Parents who never imagined they would have a reason to be in rooms like this,” he said, as he made reference to parents who believe their children have died as a result of online harm.

He also told the companies to be more helpful to parents who are seeking access to their children’s smartphones and social media accounts to help them understand what they were doing online.

“For many parents, even though their child killed themselves, they’ve had to wait years – in some instances, eight years – to get access to their child’s phone,” Harry said. “Because of the company’s privacy policies, the parents were blocked from finding out how their child died. That cannot be right.”

The trip to Brussels comes after Markle’s father was arrested Friday morning by federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material .

Thomas Markle Sr. was arrested on a federal criminal complaint alleging he kept child sexual abuse material, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with prepubescent girls, in two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for nearly two decades, according to the FBI .

Markle Sr. is charged with one count of possession of child pornography and made his initial appearance Friday in United States District Court in the Middle District of Florida in Tampa.

After his arrest in Polk County, Markle Sr. appeared in federal court in Tampa and was released back to a senior care center with the condition that he be electronically monitored, according to The Associated Press.

U.S. Magistrate Judge Lindsay Griffin also ordered a psychiatric exam, saying Markle Sr. might be unable to understand the proceedings or properly assist his lawyer.

“Mr. Markle is accused of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs depicting himself with minor girls,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “These allegations are extremely serious, and we will prosecute Mr. Markle to the fullest extent of federal law.”

FBI special agents searched two storage units registered to Markle Sr., who has rented the units in Los Angeles since 2008, with his most recent payments on both made last month by auto-pay, according to the FBI.

If convicted, Markle Sr. would face a statutory maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison, according to the FBI.

Markle Sr.’s arrest comes after The Sun , a British tabloid newspaper, reported that Meghan’s half-brother allegedly found images while cleaning out the home of their father in the Philippines.

Meghan’s father denied the allegations against him in a statement to the Daily Mail , saying, “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me.”

“I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of,” he added.

The Duchess of Sussex said she was “deeply distressed” by allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images had been found at her estranged father’s former home.

— With files from the Associated Press

scraped.title: MTR vows cooperation with gov't after reports of underfilled pillars
scraped.description: Hong Kong's railway operator, the MTR Corporation, has announced that it will cooperate with a government probe into a construction fault, after local media reported that up to 30 concrete pillars at the new Tung Chung West Station were found to be underfilled.
scraped.author: Irene Chan
scraped.h1: MTR pledges cooperation with gov’t after reports of underfilled pillars at Tung Chung West Station
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

Hong Kong’s railway operator, the MTR Corporation, has announced that it will cooperate with a government probe into a construction fault, after local media reported that up to 30 concrete pillars at the new Tung Chung West Station were found to be underfilled.

The MTR Corporation said in a response issued on Monday that it had noticed issues with “certain pillars,” which were being constructed by contractors on the platform level of the new Tung Chung West Station.

The transport corporation said it had issued a non-compliance notice to the main contractor, and was pursuing the matter regarding operational errors, handling procedures, and liabilities.

Construction on Tung Chung West Station began in 2023, with the station scheduled to open in 2029.

“At present, the corporation is awaiting the contractor’s submission of a comprehensive report along with a proposed rectification plan,” the MTR Corporation said in a Chinese-language response, adding that it would fully cooperate with government departments in their investigation and submit timely reports detailing root causes, remedial plans, and follow-up actions.

In response to HKFP, the Buildings Department said it first noticed the issue on October 27 during a regular inspection and quality audit, finding two defective columns and ordering the registered structural engineer and contractor to conduct a comprehensive check.

As of last Friday, the registered structural engineer had found around 30 defective concrete pillars at the construction site, the department said.

The department also ordered the registered structural engineer to submit an incident report by mid-November.

The responses came after HK01 reported in an exclusive on Saturday that around 30 concrete pillars in the concourse of Tung Chung West Station were suspected of being improperly poured, leaving a gap of roughly 20 to 30 centimetres between the concrete and the ceiling.

“It is understood that there are 60 pillars across the entire concourse level, and about half of them show similar defects, affecting half of the concourse floor area,” the report reads.

In response to local media, the MTR Corporation confirmed on Saturday for the first time that it had found problematic columns on the platform level of Tung Chung West Station during a regular inspection.

It said it was checking all concrete pillars on the platform and concourse levels, but did not confirm whether there were any defects on the concourse level.

The Buildings Department said that Tung Chung West Station, which is now under construction, is a three-storey station comprising the ground level, the concourse level, and the platform level.

It is being constructed using the top-down method—meaning the floor slabs are cast prior to the structural columns and structural walls, the department said. Currently, the floor slabs for both the concourse and platform levels have been completed, while vertical structural elements on the platform level, including columns and structural walls, are under construction.

“As the temporary falsework supporting the floor slab has not yet been removed, the defective columns pose no danger to the station’s structural integrity,” the department said.

scraped.title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
scraped.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.
scraped.author: AFP
scraped.h1: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China.

The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions.

Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs).

These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence.

ChatGPT’s 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further.

With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia’s market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion — currently on par with Apple as the world’s two most valuable companies.

Washington bans the export of Nvidia’s top-end “Blackwell” and “Rubin” GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications.

The policy also allows the United States’s top AI labs to maintain their global lead.

Huang has lobbied the US government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives.

This year Washington eased controls on Nvidia’s previously banned — and less powerful — “H200” chip, with the United States taking a 25 percent cut of sales.

But US conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum.

Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on US rivals.

“Chinese vendors are still using cutting-edge Nvidia chips to train their models” despite the controls, Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst at Omdia, told AFP.

Chips may be smuggled into the country, or accessed through a loophole that allows Chinese firms to rent out computing power at data centres stuffed with Nvidia chips in a third nation, often Southeast Asian.

“US export controls restrict where a chip is shipped, not who uses it,” explained Stephen Wu, founder of the Carthage Capital investment fund.

That means Nvidia GPUs can sit in Malaysia’s Johor region, for example, “in full compliance while a customer in Shenzhen logs in”, Wu told AFP.

White House adviser Michael Kratsios said this summer that Moonshot AI had accessed high-end Nvidia chips in Thailand.

See also: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese tech executive accused of spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang?

Washington has also accused Chinese AI labs of training systems to mimic the capabilities of US models.

And then there is the big question of smuggling.

Tech outlet The Information said in December that DeepSeek developed its new model using thousands of chips dismantled overseas and brought into China.

DeepSeek did not respond to a comment request at the time. Nvidia told The Information they had not seen evidence of such smuggling which “seems far-fetched”.

“Nvidia chips still make top-level AI work faster and easier, but they are no longer the only path,” said Poe Zhao, founder of analysis publication Hello China Tech.

“The open question is cost” as “training on Chinese chips usually takes more time and more engineering”.

Huawei is China’s top Nvidia competitor, although it lags behind the US titan, and DeepSeek will reportedly train its next major AI model on Huawei chips.

“Chinese-made chips are improving fast”, Su said, with more collaborations likely to come.

Huawei said in September its next-generation AI chip would be ready in the first quarter of 2027, three quarters earlier than planned.

To boost the power of Chinese-made chips, AI companies need to use more of them, Wu said.

“They pay for it in power and cost — which they can afford, because Chinese electricity is cheap and the chips are state-subsidised.”

scraped.title: HK indie book fair urges transparency after 5 exhibitors excluded
scraped.description: Organisers of an independent Hong Kong book fair have called for openness and transparency after five exhibitors were allegedly barred by authorities without explanation.
scraped.author: Hans Tse
scraped.h1: Independent Hong Kong book fair urges transparency after 5 exhibitors barred under ‘force majeure’
scraped.body_text:
Hong Kong Free Press HKFP

Hong Kong news, breaking updates – 100% Independent, impartial, non-profit

Organisers of an independent Hong Kong book fair have called for openness and transparency after five exhibitors were allegedly barred by authorities without explanation.

Duk6 Duk6, an “indie narrative book fest” that promotes self-published works, is set to hold its fourth edition on November 14 and 15 at The Mills in Tsuen Wan. This year’s fair will feature about 125 exhibitors showcasing comics, novels, zines, animation and games, according to Yun Hyun, a non-profit collective of local creators.

But organisers said over the weekend that five exhibitors had been disqualified from the event due to “force majeure.”

“We recently received notifications from relevant authorities stating that, owing to force majeure issues arising during the licensing process, certain exhibitors cannot participate,” Yun Hyun said in a social media post written in Chinese, without specifying the government departments involved.

Force majeure – a contract clause covering events beyond the parties’ control – is a staple of venue and event contracts. Yet for many in Hong Kong in recent years, the phrase has increasingly become shorthand for covert political pressure and censorship .

Yun Hyun did not name the exhibitors that had to withdraw, only saying that the affected exhibitors included comic and novel writers and illustrators. The themes of their works range from local Hong Kong culture to science fiction, the group added.

The group also called on the authorities to provide clarity regarding censorship, so that event organisers can better cooperate.

“In recent years, similar events have frequently encountered similar situations. It is hoped that relevant departments will have a more open and transparent mechanism to make it easier for creators and organisers to cooperate,” Yun Hyun said.

A curator of the fair, speaking on condition of anonymity citing fear of reprisals, told HKFP that organisers had been seeking a Temporary Places of Public Entertainment Licence from the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD). The application had to go through multiple departments for vetting, the curator said.

“One department called and told us that either these five exhibitors had to be removed, or the whole event would be cancelled, without giving any explanation,” the curator said.

HKFP has reached out to the FEHD for comment.

The curator added that the last edition of the book fair, held in early 2025, also encountered censorship against specific exhibitors by venue management.

“Given that experience, and seeing how every similar event lately has faced the same roadblocks, we were of course braced for it,” the curator said. “Still, we never imagined five exhibitors would be DQ’d [disqualified] in one go.”

The curator said all 125 exhibitors were hand-picked to ensure no AI-generated or plagiarised material was featured, adding that the event’s layout was drafted to bring like-minded artists together.

Losing five exhibitors at this stage added significantly to the team’s workload in vetting replacements and threatened to disrupt the carefully planned layout, the curator said.

The sudden exclusions also dealt a heavy blow to the vendors, who had spent months preparing to debut new work at the event, the curator said.

“Actually everyone wants to continue, but we don’t know where the line is drawn,” the curator said. “And we are not even trying to cross any lines, but even harmless things could be DQ’d.”

“The economic environment in recent years has been poor, and coupled with the impact of AI, the entire creative community is facing great challenges,” the curator added.

“As organisers, we hope that every creator and their work can be seen. But there’s only so much we can do.”

Published - November 11, 2026 01:50 am IST - MUNICH

Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany. File | Photo Credit: Reuters

Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has returned to the club’s training ground for the first time since he collapsed during practice last month. Bayern also revealed he suffered a shoulder injury.

The 40-year-old Kompany had medical treatment scheduled at the Säbener Strasse complex as he took another step toward his planned return after the international break.

“Vincent Kompany is on the road to recovery and has been back at the training ground at Säbener Strasse since the start of the week,” the club said on Tuesday. “The FC Bayern head coach is also completing rehab on his injured shoulder there. Kompany was under medical care recently, with assistant coach Aaron Danks filling in.”

Bayern had no team training on Tuesday with most of the players away. The team’s next game is at home to Cologne in the Bundesliga on Nov. 20.

Bayern powerbroker Uli Hoeness said on Sunday that Kompany would return in time for that match.

Kompany collapsed while observing a training session on Oct. 23 and was hospitalized for meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He had been dealing with a viral infection and hip injury.

Danks took charge of the team while Kompany was away and oversaw wins against Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz with the only blot a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund in der Klassiker on October 31.

Published - November 11, 2026 01:34 am IST - NEW DELHI

Indian women’s hockey goalkeeper Savita Punia. File | Photo Credit: PTI

Veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia has been rested from the Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal, replaced by Bansari Solanki in the Indian women's hockey squad unveiled on Tuesday, with head coach Sjoerd Marijne also announcing changes to the roles of some players during the event.

The tournament is scheduled to be held from November 19 to 28 at the newly-built International Sports Complex, Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal and India will enter as the defending champions. India will begin their campaign against Malaysia on the opening day of the competition.

Mid-fielder Salima Tete will continue to lead the team, which is playing its first international tournament after the historic gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month.

The hosts have secured the ACT title in 2016, 2023 and 2024.

The six-team competition will feature India, China, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand and South Korea. Like India, South Korea too have won the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy three times.

The 25-year-old Bansari has been part of the squad that won the Asia Cup last year. Bichu Devi Kharibam retained her place as the other custodian in the squad.

"This is the moment I want to give other players the chance to showcase their talent on the international stage. Some players will be playing in different positions than they normally do, so that I can see how they perform in a different role," said Marijne.

"We are excited to play in front of the home crowd and finish the year well," he added.

As part of the role shuffling, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal, who played as a forward in the Asian Games, has been named in the mid-field for the ACT. Similarly, mid-fielder Nikki Pradhan is part of the defensive line-up, while Ishika Chaudhary has been moved from defence to mid-field.

The ACT will follow a round-robin format, with each team playing the other five once. The top four teams at the end of the league stage will qualify for the semi-finals.

The opening day will see Asia's top-ranked team China take on Thailand in the tournament opener before the India-Malaysia clash following an opening ceremony.

The Indian team will then face South Korea on November 21, Thailand on November 22, China on November 24 and Japan on November 25.

The semi-finals will be played on November 27 and the medal matches on November 28.

With the home crowd behind them, the Indian team will look to deliver another strong performance and continue their winning momentum.

"The Women's Asian Champions Trophy Bhopal 2026 is an important opportunity for our team to carry forward the momentum of their historic Asian Games triumph," said Hockey India President Dilip Tirkey.

"Playing in front of home supporters will be a great motivation, and I am confident the players will put up a strong performance and make the country proud," he added.

Hockey India Secretary General, Bhola Nath Singh, also wished the team success in the tournament.

"As defending champions, the team will be determined to maintain its winning momentum. We look forward to an exciting competition and strong support from hockey fans across Madhya Pradesh," said the Secretary General.

Goalkeepers: Bansari Solanki, Bichu Devi Kharibam.

Defenders: Nikki Pradhan, Jyoti, Jyoti Singh, Sushila Chanu, Lalthantluangi, Pooja Sahoo

Mid-fielders: Rutuja Dadaso Pisal, Sunelita Toppo, Salima Tete (c), Neha, Sakshi Rana, Baljeeet Kaur, Ishika.

Forwards: Navneet Kaur, Deepika, Beauty Dungdung, Lalremsiami, Mumtaz Khan.

‘Transparency is not an assault on minority rights’ | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto

The proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, have triggered strong reactions from civil society organisations, Opposition parties and Christian institutions. The concerns are not without substance. What it seeks is tighter regulation of foreign-funded organisations, including provisions concerning assets created or acquired through foreign contributions. The Government maintains that the objective is greater transparency, accountability and prevention of misuse of foreign funds, while critics fear possible restrictions on legitimate civil society activity and minority institutions being disproportionately affected. With the Bill referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for further scrutiny, there is an opportunity for a reasoned debate.

Foreign contribution cannot become a pretext for suppressing legitimate charitable, educational, health care or social-service activity. At the same time, the receipt and utilisation of foreign funds cannot be placed beyond scrutiny.

items.title: Odakyu Unveils New Romancecar With Giant Circular Windows
items.summary: Odakyu Electric Railway unveiled images of its next-generation Romancecar limited express train on November 10, revealing a striking blue-green design featuring enormous circular windows that will allow passengers to enjoy panoramic views from ceiling to floor when the new trains enter service in March 2029. (News On Japan)

scraped.title: Odakyu Unveils New Romancecar With Giant Circular Windows
scraped.description: Odakyu Electric Railway unveiled images of its next-generation Romancecar limited express train on November 10, revealing a striking blue-green design featuring enormous circular windows that will allow passengers to enjoy panoramic views from ceiling to floor when the new trains enter service in March 2029.
scraped.author: News On Japan
scraped.h1: Odakyu Unveils New Romancecar With Giant Circular Windows
scraped.body_text:
TOKYO - Odakyu Electric Railway unveiled images of its next-generation Romancecar limited express train on November 10, revealing a striking blue-green design featuring enormous circular windows that will allow passengers to enjoy panoramic views from ceiling to floor when the new trains enter service in March 2029.

According to Odakyu, the new Romancecar has been designed around the theme of water, with a distinctive blue-green exterior and observation seating at both the front and rear of the train, continuing a signature feature of the Romancecar series. The new design places windows lower than on previous models, making it easier for young children to enjoy the passing scenery. Among the most distinctive features are large circular windows measuring 1.8 meters in diameter, offering expansive views that stretch from the ceiling down to passengers' feet. The interior will also introduce new seating arrangements, including group seating for four passengers and wider, more spacious seats measuring approximately 60 centimeters across, designed to provide greater comfort during journeys. The new train will be the first addition to the Romancecar lineup in 11 years, with commercial operations scheduled to begin in March 2029. The new Romancecar is expected to serve the popular route between Tokyo's Shinjuku Station and Hakone-Yumoto, one of Japan's leading hot spring destinations, with the trains designed to continue beyond Odawara onto the Hakone Tozan Line. Odakyu has not yet announced the full operating schedule or confirmed whether the new model will also serve other routes within its limited express network, which currently includes services to Fujisawa and Katase-Enoshima on the Shonan coast. The journey from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto takes approximately 80 to 90 minutes, carrying passengers from central Tokyo through the western suburbs and into the increasingly mountainous landscape of Kanagawa Prefecture. The route offers views of rivers, farmland and distant mountain ranges, with Mount Fuji visible from some sections in favorable weather. The new train's expansive windows are expected to make the changing scenery a central part of the travel experience. Hakone is particularly popular for its hot springs, mountain scenery and views of Mount Fuji. Visitors arriving at Hakone-Yumoto can continue into the mountains using the Hakone Tozan Railway, cable cars and the Hakone Ropeway, which passes over the volcanic landscape of Owakudani. Other attractions include Lake Ashi, where sightseeing boats offer views of Mount Fuji on clear days, the Hakone Open-Air Museum and the historic Hakone Shrine. The wider Romancecar network also connects Tokyo with the coastal resort area of Enoshima, known for its beaches, island shrine, sea caves and views across Sagami Bay. Nearby Kamakura, accessible by connecting railway services, is another major sightseeing destination, famous for its Great Buddha, historic temples and traditional streets. Whether the new 80000 series will operate on the Enoshima route has yet to be confirmed. The introduction of the new trains is expected to strengthen the appeal of Odakyu's sightseeing services, particularly for overseas visitors seeking convenient access to destinations outside Tokyo. With observation seating at both ends, large circular windows and new group seating arrangements, the company is placing greater emphasis on making the railway journey itself part of the tourist experience.

Odakyu has not yet announced the full operating schedule or confirmed whether the new model will also serve other routes within its limited express network, which currently includes services to Fujisawa and Katase-Enoshima on the Shonan coast.

The journey from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto takes approximately 80 to 90 minutes, carrying passengers from central Tokyo through the western suburbs and into the increasingly mountainous landscape of Kanagawa Prefecture. The route offers views of rivers, farmland and distant mountain ranges, with Mount Fuji visible from some sections in favorable weather. The new train's expansive windows are expected to make the changing scenery a central part of the travel experience.

Hakone is particularly popular for its hot springs, mountain scenery and views of Mount Fuji. Visitors arriving at Hakone-Yumoto can continue into the mountains using the Hakone Tozan Railway, cable cars and the Hakone Ropeway, which passes over the volcanic landscape of Owakudani. Other attractions include Lake Ashi, where sightseeing boats offer views of Mount Fuji on clear days, the Hakone Open-Air Museum and the historic Hakone Shrine.

The wider Romancecar network also connects Tokyo with the coastal resort area of Enoshima, known for its beaches, island shrine, sea caves and views across Sagami Bay. Nearby Kamakura, accessible by connecting railway services, is another major sightseeing destination, famous for its Great Buddha, historic temples and traditional streets. Whether the new 80000 series will operate on the Enoshima route has yet to be confirmed.

The introduction of the new trains is expected to strengthen the appeal of Odakyu's sightseeing services, particularly for overseas visitors seeking convenient access to destinations outside Tokyo. With observation seating at both ends, large circular windows and new group seating arrangements, the company is placing greater emphasis on making the railway journey itself part of the tourist experience.

Source: FNN

A powerful cold air mass brought the lowest temperatures of the season to much of Japan on Tuesday, November 10, with Hokkaido recording a nationwide seasonal low of minus 11.8 degrees Celsius, heavy snowfall covering northern communities, and Tokyo experiencing midwinter conditions as temperatures fell sharply across the country.

Odakyu Electric Railway unveiled images of its next-generation Romancecar limited express train on November 10, revealing a striking blue-green design featuring enormous circular windows that will allow passengers to enjoy panoramic views from ceiling to floor when the new trains enter service in March 2029.

As of 3 a.m. on November 10, Typhoon No. 32 was moving northeast over waters south of Japan, with the powerful storm expected to approach the Ogasawara Islands late Tuesday through Wednesday morning, November 11, bringing strong winds, heavy rain and waves exceeding 6 meters in some areas.

A male bear weighing approximately 270 kilograms was killed by hunters in Iwamizawa, Hokkaido, on November 8th after being caught in a box trap, with local hunters suspecting it was responsible for a series of attacks on a nearby poultry farm that left more than 100 chickens and ducks dead since August.

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early on November 8th, registering an upper 5 on Japan's seismic intensity scale in Aichi Prefecture and injuring at least 21 people, while damaging buildings and disrupting Shinkansen and conventional railway services across the region.

Hokkaido's transportation network faced further disruptions on Tuesday, November 10, as freezing temperatures, lingering snow and icy conditions caused train cancellations, flight delays and highway restrictions, although conditions improved in several areas during the afternoon.

Japan's younger generation is increasingly turning away from driving and car ownership, with the number of driver's license holders aged 24 and under falling by approximately 590,000 over the past decade to around 5.15 million in 2025, reflecting changing attitudes toward transportation, spending and the traditional appeal of owning a car.

A field of approximately 20,000 cosmos flowers has reached peak bloom at Nagai Botanical Garden in Osaka's Higashisumiyoshi Ward, where a limited-time installation by art collective teamLab is transforming the autumn landscape into a glowing display of light and sound after dark.

Sapporo deployed its distinctive Sasara snow-clearing tram for the first time this season early on November 7th, the second-earliest deployment in 10 years, after snowfall reached 8 centimeters at 4 a.m., prompting a vehicle to leave its depot to clear snow from the city's streetcar tracks.

East Japan Railway (JR East) opened its Haneda Airport Access Line construction site to the media on November 6, offering a glimpse of a major underground railway project that will connect Haneda Airport directly with central Tokyo, with services scheduled to begin in fiscal 2031.

Residents of Awaji Island, one of the Kansai region's most popular resort destinations, are facing growing disruption from vacation rentals, with complaints involving late-night drinking, outdoor barbecues, fireworks, illegal parking and garbage disposal violations, while one property operator has been accused of destroying a warning sign installed by neighbors.
